patch_description:
The current approach relies purely on random spherical starts, which rarely land in the basin of the optimal 14-point arrangement (known squared ratio ≈ 1/4.1658 ≈ 0.24003). For N=14 on/in a sphere, good configurations are highly structured (e.g., an icosahedral 12-point shell plus 2 poles, or hexagonal-bipyramid-like arrangements). Two changes:

1. Add structured initial guesses (icosahedron vertices + 2 poles, cube+octahedron+poles, anti-prism based) as candidate starts in addition to random ones — these start much closer to the optimum and converge to better local optima.

2. Use a two-phase restart budget per the recommendation: first pass with cheap maxiter to rank candidates, then fully converge only the top few. This keeps runtime near the current 1.2s while exploring more starts.

This should push the squared ratio from ~0.21 toward ~0.24, raising combined_score from 0.89 toward 1.0.
